LLM auditresponse for 001-fix-install.patch:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided patch modifies a CMake script used in the build process of the mc-schem package. It changes the installation directive from `install(FILES ...)` to `install(PROGRAMS ...)`, and adjusts the destination directory for the binary based on whether the target is a Windows DLL or a Unix shared library.

This change ensures correct installation behavior for executable binaries by using `PROGRAMS`, which is more appropriate than `FILES` for binaries meant to be executed. The patch also corrects the installation path on non-Windows systems to place the shared library in `CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR` instead of `CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR`, which is the standard location for libraries. These are legitimate packaging adjustments consistent with cross-platform CMake practices.

There are no network operations, obfuscated commands, or suspicious file manipulations. The changes are confined to standard CMake directives and do not introduce any malicious behavior.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Benign CMake installation path fix</summary>
</security_assessment>
